newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe finds nearby US soybeans too hot to handle.
newsitem.headline: Europe finds nearby US soybeans too hot to handle.

text.p: The rise in U.S. soybean prices has taken them beyond the reach of European physical traders, who prefer to quote Brazilian equivalents at much lower levels.

Sellers in Europe say nearby U.S. soybeans become unsellable every year at this time, and the situation is reversed later on in the season. For positions October through to March, sellers prefer quoting U.S. beans rather than South American ones.
On the Chicago futures market soybeans for July delivery are trading at around $8.30 a bushel against $6.80 for November.
Depending on market conditions, physical traders may quote U.S. material at this time of the year, but they still attract a hefty premium over Brazilian beans.
On Thursday U.S. beans were quoted at $330 a tonne cif Rotterdam against $317.50 for their Brazilian equivalents.
